# MCP Contributor Field Guide

> A practical guide to landing a contribution in the modelcontextprotocol
> GitHub org (go-sdk, python-sdk, typescript-sdk, servers, inspector). Written
> for humans and agents. The core insight: the org is saturated, so do not race
> existing issues. Strike first on fresh bugs or discover your own, verify the
> premise and the claim status before investing, and keep changes small and
> reproduced.

## Start here

- [README](./README.md): overview and reading order.
- [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md): step-by-step instructions for an LLM/agent contributor.

## Guide

- [Finding work that is actually open](./guide/01-finding-work.md): why the
  bulk "is it claimed?" text search undercounts, the reliable per-issue timeline
  check, the `ready for work` magnet trap, and the strike-first approach.
- [Per-repo playbook](./guide/02-repo-playbook.md): which repos accept PRs vs
  issues only (inspector is issues-only), branch and label conventions, and the
  build/test command for each SDK.
- [Opening a PR without tripping](./guide/03-opening-a-pr.md): commit and PR
  style, the fork-behind-upstream `workflow`-scope push rejection and the
  cherry-pick-onto-fork-main workaround.
- [Finding and verifying bugs](./guide/04-finding-and-verifying-bugs.md): a
  12-class bug taxonomy for an MCP SDK, how to reproduce each class, and the
  premise-scrutiny that prevents "working as intended" closes.

## Key external references

- modelcontextprotocol org: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol
- MCP spec (latest revision): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification
- MCP registry (publish community servers): https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry

## One-line rules

- Check an issue is unclaimed with the timeline API, not a text search.
- `ready for work` issues are usually the MOST contested, not the least.
- inspector does not accept external PRs; open a detailed issue instead.
- Verify a bug's premise against code AND spec before writing a fix.
- Reproduce every bug with a runnable test before claiming it.
- Keep PRs small, tested, and low-noise; protect the maintainer's trust.
